verdict:
Train at 1c9e2c2, mean 5.75. Only a little better than r2 (5.62), and not yet at fern level. Seat is still the best frame: a large, clean stone profile, the head peaking at 214 Rec.709 luma, with the window dark behind it. The aisle now works as a lit island. Dawn's face measures about 161-165 mean and 179 peak, against an aisle floor of about 27-30 and ceiling panels of about 15-17, and her head turns into her own window. The builder's claim holds: no pixel reaches 250 in any frame, raw or graded (graded luma maxima 217 aisle, 214 seat, 171 rack). Pixels under 8/255 luma are 8.6%, 11.4% and 10.0%, which is fine.

Three things hold the stage back.
(1) The reflection in seat reads as a second passenger in a cap, not as Dawn. It faces the same way she does (frame left), because in seat her head looks only about 8 degrees into the glass. The reflected bun is still dark (about 24, against a dome of 43 and a face of 44; r2 asked for at least 35), so blurred it shows as the peak of a cap. No light crosses its face, so nothing in the image proves it is in the glass.
(2) Rack is not a controlled close-up. The case fills only about a quarter of the frame width (x 65-395), pushed into the top-left corner with its handle about 42 px from the top edge. Dawn's head is cut by the bottom edge at the brow and eyes, which the brief's framing rule bans.
(3) The carriage is underdressed and too clean: identical rows of seats, only Dawn's case on the near racks, nothing personal anywhere. The near-right window sits at about 8.5 mean, against 12-20 for the left windows, and its two passing streaks barely register. Several passing lights also read as shelves rather than motion. The streak shader already tapers along its length, but long streaks are cut square by the window edges (the three even bars at seat right, x 985-1170) and by the frame edge.

On hardware, the side keeper now covers the old pull. But the two wheel hubs on the case's far end render as curled bright hooks. Enlarged, they read as numerals: a '9' above, and a '3' or '2' below. The lower one is the brightest pixel in the rack frame (171). Two faint pale marks also peek out just past the keeper's edge on the pocket side. Under the no-letter-like rule, these still need covering.
answers:
1. Aisle eyeline: mostly yes. Her nose points at her own window, and the gaze lands on dark glass with the orange streak at y about 487, so a viewer reads 'turned to the window'. It is marginal, though. The head is only about 55 px from crown to chin, with blank statue eyes, her body is square to the lens, and the lit pale wall pier at x 100-150 pulls the eye just past the glass. It also breaks continuity with seat. apply_camera re-aims her head per camera: AISLE_LOOK in the aisle, about 42 degrees into the glass, and LOOK in seat. LOOK sits 2.8 m ahead and only 0.06 m beyond the glass, about 8 degrees into it, so in seat she looks along the carriage, parallel to the glass, not out of it. In seat she does not read as looking out.

2. Reflection as Dawn through the moving lights: no.
- Direction: the ghost faces frame-left, the same way as Dawn. With her gaze only about 8 degrees into the glass, the mirror flips just a small x-component.
- The cap read: the dome (43) and face (44) match in value, but the bun is dark (24), and blurred it reads as the peak of a cap. Its shoulders and a seat back behind it make it a second traveller seated at the glass.
- Light: keep_clear removes every random streak that crosses an ellipse around the reflection. One warm streak stops at its forehead (y about 288), and the only light crossing it is the cool hero bar at y about 600 across its chest. Nothing passes through the face, which is what would prove it is a reflection.
- Level: fine. It is about 2.2 times the glass around it (44 against 18-21) and about 27% of her own face (164), inside r1's 40% limit.

3. Rack as part of the carriage: partly. The rack rail, the rounded window reveal, curtains, linen-topped seats, a far traveller and a strip light at top right all match the aisle. But the seven aluminium bars read as one dark band: only the front rail's highlight separates, with two faint lines at the left. Case continuity holds. Like for like, its pocket face measures about 72-76 in aisle and 76-79 in rack, and its dark end about 22 in both. So the bag_mute switch, r2's fix for the zip pull that read as a '3', does not change how the case reads. The linen covers do change per camera (linen_tone 0.55 in aisle, 1.0 elsewhere), but that is r2's deliberate aisle trim. Dawn's head, cut at the brow and eyes by the bottom edge, makes the frame feel like a slip rather than a chosen close-up.

4. Plain case hardware.
- Aisle: clean. At about 85 px across, the case shows only the dark keeper and a dim pull mark at the lower right of the pocket, nothing letter-like.
- Rack: the keeper reads as a plain fabric tab, and the two bottom zip pulls are plain metal. But two faint pale marks remain just past the keeper's pocket-side edge (frame about x 167-175, y 170-192): a small ring, and a fainter mark above it.
- Rack: the two wheel hubs on the case's far end (about 390,95 and 392,257) render as bright curled hooks. Enlarged, the upper reads as a '9' and the lower as a '3' or '2'. The lower one is the brightest point in the frame. Cover them.

5. Zero luminance above 250: confirmed. Per-channel maxima are 225/219/182 graded and 249/224/246 raw (aisle, seat, rack), and no pixel reaches 250 in any channel of any frame. Note that rack's brightest point (171 luma) is the lower wheel hub, the letter-like mark. Once the hubs are covered, the case peaks at about 149 on its pocket face, and nothing gives it an edge highlight.

fixes.problem: The reflection faces the same way as Dawn, so it reads as a second person beside her. In seat she looks along the carriage, only about 8 degrees into the glass, not out of the window.
fixes.fix:
Give her one head pose in all three cuts, turned about 40 degrees into the glass.
- Set LOOK = AISLE_LOOK (GLASS_X - 1.2, SEAT_Y - 1.6, 1.12), call aim_head(s, LOOK, base_turn=(-10, -22)) in place_dawn(), and delete the re-aim branch in apply_camera.
- Expected result, from the code's geometry (eyes at about x -1.19, glass at -1.53, camera at eyes + SEAT_CAM_OFFSET): the reflection turns about 36 degrees off the lens, a three-quarter face with the bun at its side, as r1 asked. Dawn herself sits about 18 degrees past profile, away from the lens, so she reads as looking out.
- Do not go to 55-60 degrees (LOOK at GLASS_X - 1.6, SEAT_Y - 1.0) with the camera at (0.70, -0.42). That leaves the reflection only about 13 degrees off the lens, and a nearly frontal reflection hides the bun behind the skull, which is r1's 'bald stranger' fault.
- Optional: SEAT_CAM_OFFSET = (0.70, -0.42, 0.05) with the 42-degree pose gives a reflection about 31 degrees off the lens, Dawn about 11 degrees past profile, and a slightly wider gap between them.
- bun_rim and hair_glass are aimed at fixed offsets from her eyes that assume a head facing down the carriage (bun at +0.12 y). Re-aim them at the bun's new position.
- Check that the hands still rest in her lap.

fixes.problem: Dawn's head is cut by the bottom frame edge at the brow and eyes. The case sits in the top-left corner at about a quarter of the frame width, with its handle about 42 px from the top. It is not a controlled close-up.
fixes.fix:
Tighten on the case: CAMERAS['rack'] loc (0.20, SEAT_Y - 1.05, 1.92), lens 40 -> 55, aim about (-1.20, SEAT_Y + 0.60, 1.95).
- Expected result, by back-projection from the current frame (pinhole, 36 mm sensor): the case at about x 100-590 (38% of the width), its handle about 80 px below the top and its foot near y 490, with the racks receding to the right.
- Do not use the aim (-1.05, SEAT_Y + 0.75, 1.88). It projects the handle to about 10 px from the top and cuts the case's near end at the left edge.
- This framing drops Dawn out of frame (her crown projects below y 1000). That reverses r2's request and the builder's 'Include Dawn below the rack' commit, so decide it knowingly.
- If her crown must stay: keep the current loc at lens 45 with aim about (-1.00, SEAT_Y + 0.80, 1.75). The case sits at x 85-435 with its handle still about 48 px from the top, the crown is in frame and the brow just below the bottom edge. The margin is thin, so test-render it.
- Either way, never cut through the eyes.

fixes.problem: No passing light crosses the reflected face, so nothing proves the ghost is in the glass. The reflected bun is dark (about 24, against a dome of 43 and a face of 44), and blurred it reads as the peak of a cap.
fixes.fix:
Add one HERO_STREAKS entry through the reflection's lower face (hero streaks bypass keep_clear): offset (0.0, -0.02, -0.07), dist 18.0, length about 4.5, height 0.025, rgb (1.0, 0.62, 0.3), k 1.2. Keep it dim enough that the face shows through.
- Position: a glass offset maps to about 1.3 times that distance on the reflected head here. So -0.035 would cross near the nose, and -0.07 to -0.075 nearer the mouth and jaw. Check in the frame.
- Length: keep it short. A 10 m streak at 18 m spans roughly x 170-830 and would run into her real brow at about x 700, the same tangent r2 removed from her nose. Its right-hand taper must die out before about x 640.
- Don't add a streak 'behind' the bun to silhouette it. A reflection is additive, so a light beyond the glass cannot outline it.
- Set TRIMS['seat']['hair_glass'] = 1.4 so the reflected bun reaches r2's target of at least 35. Keep the reflected dome within about 1.1 times the face, and the real crown no brighter than now (dome mean about 142).
- Do this after fix 1, which changes how the bun faces the glass.

fixes.problem: The two wheel hubs on the case's far end render as curled bright hooks that, enlarged, read as numerals ('9', and '3' or '2'). The lower one is the brightest point in the frame (171). Two faint pale marks also peek out just past the keeper's pocket-side edge. These are letter-like marks.
fixes.fix:
In rack_case(), cover each wheel hub with a plain disc parented to the shell, the same way as the keeper: sk.cyl radius about 0.024, depth 0.006, in the 'matte charcoal zipper keeper' material (0.021, 0.023, 0.026), rough 0.89, with its axis along the hub. The hubs sit at about (390, 95) and (392, 257) in the 1280 rack frame.
- Keeper: the pale marks reach about 2-9 px past its pocket-side edge. At the keeper's scale (about 2.3 mm/px) that is up to about 20 mm, so widening it to 0.066 with a 4 mm shift covers only about 8 mm. Widen the keeper from 0.057 to about 0.08 toward the pocket side, shift its centre about 12 mm that way, and keep it clear of the case corner.
- Then measure from the 1280 frame: no 3x3 px cluster on the case above 1.6 times its local mean, except the zip sliders.

fixes.problem: Several passing lights read as shelves or rails rather than lights smeared by motion. The three even, parallel bars at seat right (x 985-1170, y about 190, 295 and 325) start and stop square. The cool hero bar at y about 600 lies across the reflection's chest like a grab rail.
fixes.fix:
The shader is not the cause. train_mats.streak already tapers along its length (ramp up over the first 35%, down over the last 45%, squared) and is Gaussian across, and outside() already varies hgt about threefold.
- Cause: the streaks are far longer than the openings (up to about 37 m at d 55), so the window piers, the reveal and the frame edge cut them square.
- In outside(), cap length at about 1.5-2 times the visible width of a pane at that distance, and draw about a third of them short (1.2-2.5 m), so most tapered ends fall inside the glass.
- Break up the seat-right trio, with a different seed or by removing one, so they are not evenly spaced and equal.
- Hero streak 1 (the bar at y about 600, length 3.2 m at 6 m): shorten it to about 1.5-2 m, or push it to dist 12-15, so it thins and tapers within the glass.
- Optional: add a 10-20% low-frequency ripple along x in the shader.

fixes.problem: Set dressing is thin and too clean: identical rows of seats, only Dawn's case on the near racks, nothing personal anywhere. The near-right window sits at about 8.5 mean against 12-20 for the left windows, and its two passing streaks barely show.
fixes.fix:
Dressing:
- Add 4-5 st.holdall bags at mixed sizes and muted tints on the racks at rows 6 and beyond, both sides. Keep them smaller and lighter than her case and out of the bays next to hers, as luggage() intends.
- Hang a coat over one seat back (R5 aisle).
- Skew two linen headrest covers by 2-4 degrees and drop one onto a seat. Vary the curtains (some half-drawn).
- Put a plain paper cup and an unlabelled bottle on the window ledge by the Sleeper (L9), or on an empty cushion. Not on a fold-down tray: the trays sit on the seat backs, which face away from this camera.
- Nothing on any prop may carry text or a logo.

Near-right window: it already has two aisle_motion streaks (indices 1 and 3: side +1, bays 1-2). Raise their strength from 7 to about 11, and add one more (side +1, bay 1, z 1.1-1.2, depth about 15). Aim for the left windows' 12-20, so the pane reads as black glass with lights passing, as the design wants, rather than a dead slab.

fixes.problem: The ceiling and cove fill the top of the frame at about 15-17 (top 45%: mean 23 including the fittings, median 19), with dark seat backs in the bottom 120 rows (mean 16). Dawn is small: about 55 px from crown to chin.
fixes.fix:
Lens 38 -> 42, and lower CAMERAS['aisle'] aim z from 2.08 to 1.92.
- The longer lens crops about 45 px of ceiling. The tilt is only about half a degree (vanishing point from about y 398 to 388), so it adds little.
- Her head grows from about 55 px to about 61 px.
- If more ceiling should go, lower the aim to about 1.75 (vanishing point about y 373), but that brings up more of the dark seat backs at the bottom.
- Check that the two burning fittings of bay 2 stay in frame (they project to about y 90 at their top) and are not cut by the top edge.

fixes.problem: The seven rack bars read as one dark band, with only the front rail's highlight separating, so the case does not read as resting across bars.
fixes.fix:
Keep the bag_mute switch. It is r2's fix for the zip pull that read as a '3' in the aisle, and the case already matches across cuts (pocket face about 72-76 in aisle and 76-79 in rack; dark end about 22 in both).
- In TRIMS['rack'], keep bag_edge at 1.0.
- Add a thin COOL area light along the bars (about 0.03 x 1.5 m, about 6 W), light-linked to the rack_bar_L* objects, so each tube catches its own thin highlight line under the case.
- Keep those lines below the case's lit pocket face (about 150 peak once the hubs are covered), so the bars do not upstage it.
